chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Jamil ibn Dirraj from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): In

for a sick person who fainted and did not regain consciousness until he reached the station (of Arafat), he said: 'A man performs ihram on his behalf.' And whoever forgot his ihram and did not remember it except after completing all the rituals, there is no penalty upon him, and his intention has sufficed for him. This was narrated.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: Ihram (the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The Station (of Arafat, a critical pillar of Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who faints before reaching Arafat or forgets to enter ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *ihram* for those incapacitated by illness or forgetfulness, emphasizing the Shia principle that intention (*niyyah*) suffices for validity when the physical act is delayed or performed by proxy. It highlights the juristic distinction between a representative entering *ihram* for an unconscious pilgrim and the individual who simply forgets the state until after completing the rituals, ensuring the pilgrimage remains valid without penalty in both cases.
